Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show 2027: Parking and Rides to WestWorld

Scottsdale Sprinters runs group transportation for the 2027 Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show and Shopping Expo, February 11 through 21 at WestWorld of Scottsdale. This guide turns the official dates and directions into a plan for exhibitors, sponsors, families and guests traveling between lodging, dinners and the showgrounds.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

Where do you park, drop off or take a rideshare at the Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show?

WestWorld of Scottsdale spreads parking across nearly 20 lots and says it depends on the day’s event, and fees may apply for certain events; the show’s 2027 parking, valet and rideshare answer is announced closer to the date, and a chauffeured ride skips the question: it unloads where event staff direct. WestWorld asks visitors to view its parking map before the visit and to follow event-day signage on arrival. Parking questions go to WestWorld at (480) 312-6802. For the 2025 show, the show’s FAQ said all of its shows have free parking, with valet priced at the valet booth; the answer for February 2027 is announced closer to the date. Neither the show nor WestWorld publishes a rideshare, shuttle or hired-vehicle drop-off area. Your chauffeur takes the entrance the show directs: the Main entrance at the large horse statue on the northbound SR-101 access road, just north of Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard; the North entrance at 94th Street and Bell Road; or the McDowell Mountain Ranch entrance, open only during show season and special events. We unload where event staff direct and come back when your group is ready. The WM Phoenix Open runs the same week, through February 14, 2027. Its 2027 parking plan is not published yet; in 2026 it used WestWorld lots for its remote parking, so allow extra time on February 11 to 14.

When and where is the 2027 Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show?

The 2027 Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show and Shopping Expo is scheduled for 11 days, February 11 through 21, at WestWorld of Scottsdale, 16601 North Pima Road; the show organizer publishes the controlling schedule, so every group should confirm its exact arena times there before setting transportation pickups. WestWorld sits in north Scottsdale beside the Loop 101 corridor, north of Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard. The official show page notes that the Pima frontage road carries northbound traffic only. That detail matters when a group estimates its final approach: a hotel may look close on a map while the legal route to the assigned entrance adds a loop and several signal cycles. The published event spans more than a week, but a rider, breeder, vendor and spectator can have entirely different daily rhythms. Treat the official class schedule, admission information and exhibitor instructions as separate planning documents. Transportation should follow the people in your party, not a generic opening time. Send the reservations team the sessions you cannot miss and any dinner or barn commitments afterward. The main show landing page and official schedule currently agree on February 11 through 21. A separate RV information page contains an inconsistent February 12 reference, which is why this guide uses the current event page and schedule rather than repeating secondary copy. Recheck the official schedule close to travel and use the final credential packet for access instructions.

How early should a group leave for WestWorld?

Plan to reach the WestWorld approach 45 minutes before the first fixed commitment, then work backward from the hotel pickup and add a 15-minute group-loading window; that buffer protects against lobby delays, Loop 101 traffic, event signage changes and the walk from the authorized unloading point to the correct arena. A chauffeured vehicle removes the parking search, but it does not remove event traffic or pedestrian controls. WestWorld states that parking and lot use depend on the day’s event and asks visitors to follow event-day signage. For that reason, a useful itinerary specifies an arrival objective such as “at the venue approach by 7:15” rather than promising a particular curb or gate that the organizer has not yet assigned. Morning exhibitors may want a quiet, direct hotel-to-showgrounds movement with no intermediate stops. Spectator groups often need a later departure, a meal stop and an evening return. Sponsors or hospitality teams may have several waves. Separate those patterns before choosing a vehicle; one oversized round trip is not always as practical as two precisely timed movements. Give every rider one published lobby time and one departure time. A group captain should count passengers, communicate with the chauffeur and alert the reservations team when the class schedule changes. Avoid building the plan around “everyone knows where to meet.” WestWorld is a large event campus, and a named on-site meeting description is more dependable than a chain of individual text messages.

Which vehicle works best for horse-show guests and teams?

Choose 1 vehicle only after counting every rider and separating personal luggage from show equipment: a 14-seat Executive Sprinter suits a focused hotel group, a 24-seat mini bus handles a larger team, and groups above that size should ask the reservations team to build a written multi-vehicle movement plan. Passenger capacity is a seating limit, not a promise about equipment space. Tack trunks, display materials, garment bags, purchases and luggage can reduce the practical rider count. List the largest items when requesting a quote so the reservations team can confirm fit in writing. Do not assume an empty passenger seat is interchangeable with a safe cargo position. The Executive Sprinter is the natural choice when the priority is a calm cabin, forward-facing travel and direct transfers for a small delegation. The mini bus is a better starting point when several hotel rooms move on the same schedule. A party-layout vehicle can work for an evening sponsor dinner, but a daytime show transfer usually benefits from an executive layout and a conservative gear plan. Browse the actual vehicles rather than selecting only by category name. The fleet pages show the published seated capacity and current hourly terms. If a group will change size during the show, tell the reservations team which days differ. A vehicle that fits eight travelers on arrival day may not fit the same people plus their collected purchases on departure day. The picker on this page sorts the fleet the way show guests ride. Breeders, buyers and VIP guests start with the Maybach Jet Sprinter, then the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter and the Suburban. Spectators and Expo friends take the Executive White Sprinter or a Limo Party Sprinter. Families and barn crews take the Executive Black Sprinter, the mini bus, the mini coach or the motorcoach.

How should exhibitors coordinate hotels, barns and evening plans?

Build each show day around 3 anchors—the first required arrival, the last nonnegotiable arena commitment and the final hotel return—then place barn visits, shopping and dinner between them; this keeps the chauffeur brief readable and prevents a flexible social stop from making the group late for a fixed class or presentation. Start with a one-page movement sheet. Include the pickup property, the group captain’s mobile number, passenger count, mobility needs, equipment notes, official session reference and requested return window. If more than one hotel is involved, list the order rather than asking the chauffeur to improvise it after boarding. The reservations team can flag an itinerary that tries to cover too much ground. A split schedule may be more efficient for teams whose responsibilities begin and end at different times. For example, barn staff can travel early while participants and guests use a later pickup. The evening plan can reunite the group for dinner. This is a coordination choice, not a claim that WestWorld permits a particular operating pattern; final unloading, staging and pickup instructions remain subject to the venue and event staff. For the return, choose a time-based meeting window and a recognizable landmark description supplied by the event, then keep the group captain reachable. A chauffeur cannot block traffic or wait in an unauthorized lane. If the assigned pickup area changes, the reservations team and captain need one clear channel so the adjustment reaches the whole party at once.

What should airport arrival and departure days include?

Allow at least 2 separate transportation plans—an airport transfer and a show-day charter—unless every traveler lands together with light luggage; flight delays, baggage collection and bulky equipment make a single tightly timed airport-to-WestWorld movement fragile, while a dedicated arrival transfer keeps the show itinerary independent and easier to revise. Collect each flight number, scheduled arrival, traveler count and luggage description before choosing the pickup structure. Travelers using Phoenix Sky Harbor may arrive at different terminals or experience different baggage delays. A consolidated transfer can still work, but the written plan needs a meeting rule and a decision point for a significantly delayed flight. Do not send unverified animal, tack or specialized cargo through a passenger booking. This page covers people and their ordinary travel belongings. Any unusual equipment must be disclosed and accepted in writing before the trip. The reservations team can confirm what the selected vehicle can safely carry and whether a separate specialist movement is necessary. Departure day deserves its own schedule. Purchases and additional bags can change the space requirement, and checkout times may not align with evening flights. A hotel storage stop, meal or final visit should be written into the requested hours. For airport specifics, use the Phoenix airport transportation page and provide the airline and flight number with the inquiry.

How does a group make the pickup plan easy to follow?

Put 6 items in the final trip brief: pickup address, lobby time, passenger count, group captain, WestWorld arrival target and return trigger; add accessibility or gear notes beside those fields, then distribute the same version to every traveler so no one relies on an outdated text thread or a different entrance assumption. The best brief is short enough to read on a phone. Use full addresses for hotels and private pickups, not just property nicknames. State whether the return is a fixed clock time or a call from the captain after a session ends. If dinner follows, include the reservation time and address so the travel window can be tested before the group leaves the hotel. WestWorld says its parking configuration depends on the event and that the campus has multiple entrances. The show’s official travel page describes the main entrance near Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard and additional approaches used from the north. Those are orientation facts, not permission for a commercial vehicle to use a specific gate. Follow the organizer’s current credential and signage instructions on the day. Keep one backup instruction: if cellular messages are delayed, the group returns to the agreed event meeting description and waits for the captain’s direction. Do not ask individual passengers to negotiate separate pickup points. One coordinated move is safer, faster and far less likely to strand someone on the opposite side of the campus.

When should transportation be reserved for the February show?

Availability varies by date and by vehicle, so no fixed lead time applies: send the 4 planning details — the show dates, the estimated passenger counts, the hotel locations and the number of movements — as soon as they are settled, and the reservations team tests hotel sequencing and event-day assumptions against them. A planning inquiry does not need every class time to be final. Begin with dates, estimated passenger counts, hotel locations and the number of movements. Mark uncertain pieces as provisional. The final reservation should still carry a confirmed written itinerary, but early scope lets the group compare one vehicle, staggered service and multi-vehicle options in writing. Availability varies by date and by vehicle. Request a current quote for your date and we confirm in writing what is open. If the show schedule changes, send the update through the group captain and ask for the revised transportation timing in writing. Do not assume a later arena start automatically shifts the chauffeur window. Vehicle and driver schedules connect across the day, so a material change must be acknowledged rather than left in a group chat. The reservations team can be reached at the site’s published phone and email. Share only the operational details needed to plan the ride. Admission, exhibitor credentials, stall arrangements and official event access come from the Arabian Horse Association of Arizona and WestWorld, not from the transportation reservation.

What do groups ask before booking horse-show transportation?

Show guests ask when and where the 2027 show runs, how admission and parking work and who owns WestWorld; groups booking a ride add 4 practical questions about what the ride includes, pickup locations, class-time changes and equipment, and the answers below keep transportation separate from what WestWorld and the show organizer decide.

Frequently asked questions

When is the Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show 2027?

Thursday, February 11 to Sunday, February 21, 2027: eleven days at WestWorld of Scottsdale. The show lists its 2028 dates as February 17 to 27, 2028.

Where is the Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show held?

At WestWorld of Scottsdale, 16601 North Pima Road, Scottsdale, AZ 85260, just north of Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard. The Pima frontage road carries northbound traffic only.

How much is admission to the Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show?

The show publishes its prices on its official site. Admission is scheduled to go on sale September 25, 2026, and Fairs.com is the only authorized seller. The show offers an 11-day show pass, an advance-only group rate for groups of 25 or more, and reserved bleacher and box seats for the Saturday evening performance; box seats open in late January or early February 2027.

Is parking free at the Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show?

The 2027 answer is announced closer to the date. For the 2025 show, the show’s FAQ said parking was free, with valet priced at the valet booth. WestWorld says its parking depends on the day’s event and fees may apply for certain events.

Who owns WestWorld in Scottsdale?

The City of Scottsdale: WestWorld says it is owned and operated by the city. The Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show held there is the Arabian Horse Association of Arizona’s event.

Does transportation include show admission or credentials?

No. Transportation covers the reserved vehicle and chauffeur only. Purchase admission and obtain exhibitor, vendor or hospitality credentials through the official Scottsdale Arabian Horse Show channels.

Can the chauffeur use any WestWorld entrance?

No entrance is promised in advance. WestWorld has multiple approaches and event-day controls; the chauffeur follows the current organizer, venue and traffic instructions for authorized unloading and pickup.

What if a class or session time changes?

The group captain should contact the reservations team promptly. A timing change is confirmed only when the revised transportation plan is acknowledged in writing.

Can tack trunks or show equipment ride in the passenger vehicle?

Only when the exact items and selected vehicle have been reviewed and confirmed in writing. Passenger capacity does not establish cargo capacity, and specialized equipment may need a separate solution.
